challenge: Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 2 (Side Hustle)

whyThisSchemaAndPrompt.problem: Single-image 3D room reconstruction tools generate visually smooth meshes that silently hallucinate occluded corners. Movers and studio tenants cannot trust a pretty 3D mesh to answer whether a 154cm Queen bed and a 140cm desk leave room for a mini-fridge or pass through a 76cm hallway door.
whyThisSchemaAndPrompt.solution: We designed RoomGraph v1.2 (`shared/roomGraphSchema.ts`) around epistemic honesty: every extracted object carries `epistemic: observed | inferred | occluded_prior` and explicit metric error bars (`posPlusMinusCm`, `dimPlusMinusCm`).
whyThisSchemaAndPrompt.promptDecision: Instead of asking Gemma 3 (`gemma3:4b`) to guess raw centimetre coordinates in a vacuum, our multi-stage compiler (`server/gemmaCompiler.ts`) forces Step 1 (`vision.calibrate`) to lock onto a standardized architectural fixture (e.g., KS standard door frame 210x82cm) before computing bounding footprints and uncertainty bands.

checkpoints.title: Designing RoomGraph v1.2 with Epistemic Status & Uncertainty Bands
checkpoints.decision: Separated `observed` (direct floor-corner visibility), `inferred` (partial occlusion + standard furniture priors), and `occluded_prior` (blind-spot inference) so downstream tools can compute both Nominal and Worst-Case feasibility.

checkpoints.title: Gemma 3 Vision Compiler + Sentry Agent Tracing Spans
checkpoints.decision: Instrumented `vision.calibrate`, `ai.run.gemma3`, `compiler.uncertainty_solver`, and `db.mongodb.upsert` with token usage and latency waterfall tracking.

checkpoints.title: Downstream #1: Moving What-If & TabPFN Cost Quantile Verifier
checkpoints.decision: Built a 2-tier geometric constraint solver: flags `UNCERTAINTY_OVERFLOW` when two items pass under nominal dimensions (e.g. 2cm gap) but collide under `±8cm` epistemic uncertainty, telling the user the exact single measurement to verify with a tape measure.
